_comment: What the 'bounded-exhausted' label actually carries, across every experiment doc that claims it. Regenerate: this census is derived from the docs themselves.
question: If bounded-exhausted means 'still partial under the nine-item DoD but low-return to continue', how many rows wearing the label say how far from the DoD they actually are?
finding: 12 of 13 name their residuals, which is the substantive core of the claim -- the work behind the label is not hollow. But only 2 of 13 reference the Definition of Done, so the label carries NO information about distance from solved. B06, the most thorough row in the phase, scores 6 of 9; a much thinner row wears the same badge. That is what makes 'bounded-exhausted' read as 'done' when it is a decision to stop.
what_it_is_NOT: This is not a finding that the rows are overclaimed. Nobody has claimed Phase 4 closed: the playbook's own frontmatter still reads status: planned, the campaign scorecard lists every family as pending or partial, and analysis/mechanics_baseline.yaml holds 96 of 107 rows at 'partial'. The label is an intermediate disposition, and it is honest about stopping. It is simply not calibrated.
cheap_fix: Require one line in every bounded-exhaustion doc: 'DoD: N of 9 met (items ...), items ... open'. It costs a sentence, it makes the label comparable across rows, and it would have prevented reading B06 at 6/9 and E16 at 2/9 as the same status.
